summary.short: Finnish statute supplementing the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689). It designates market surveillance and notifying authorities, sets up a central contact point and a sanctions board, and provides administrative fines for AI Act breaches, applying from 1 January 2026.
summary.long: Finnish statute supplementing the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689). It designates national market surveillance authorities by sector for high-risk AI systems, supervises prohibited practices and transparency duties, sets up a central contact point and a sanctions board, and regulates notifying authorities and notified bodies. It provides administrative fines for AI Act breaches by providers, authorised representatives, importers, distributors, deployers and notified bodies: up to EUR 35 million or 7% of worldwide turnover for prohibited practices, EUR 15 million or 3% for other listed breaches, and EUR 7.5 million or 1% for incorrect information; the lower amount applies to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises. Fines may be waived for minor breaches or where clearly unreasonable, and are not imposed where criminal proceedings or a final judgment exist for the same act. Parliamentary business and certain parliamentary and oversight bodies are excluded. Effective 1 January 2026.

notes: Finnish text; English glosses in brackets are annotator-supplied. Relations and entities are coded from the operative sections 1 to 29 and the cover page. None of the referenced acts is in the registry, so target_instrument_id is empty throughout. The text does not state that this Act amends, repeals or replaces any other act. Scope exclusions in 1 § cover Parliament, its Ombudsman and the Chancellor of Justice. 11 § disapplies 9 § para 1 and 10 § para 2 when the data protection ombudsman acts as notified body. Entry into force 1 January 2026 (29 §); 21 § does not apply to prohibited practices before entry into force. For micro, small and medium-sized enterprises the fine cap is the lower of the two amounts (23 § para 3). No internal inconsistency found. The not_applicable status for relations and entities is a schema placeholder; entries are present.
